changes.text: 这时的国会人很少。同一天，日志记下一个付诸表决的问题：七个州出席的国会，是否有权接受总司令的辞职？日志留下了点名表决：名单上列出的议员几乎都投赞成，帕特里奇投了反对；埃勒里的反对票，日志记为应“该议员”的请求改成了赞成，没有写明这位议员是谁。22日的出席记录是马萨诸塞、罗得岛、宾夕法尼亚、特拉华、马里兰、弗吉尼亚和北卡罗来纳七个州，另有新罕布什尔和南卡罗来纳各一名议员。到了23日接见当天，国会还议决立即写信给新罕布什尔、康涅狄格、纽约、新泽西、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚六个州的行政长官，催他们的代表马上到会：国会在此开会期间，出席的从未超过七个州，其中多数只有两名代表，而批准正式和约等几件要务都需要至少九个州同意。

Congress was thin at the time. The same day, the journal records a question put to the vote: "Is it the sense of Congress that seven states in Congress Assembled are competent to receive the resignation of a Commander in Chief?" The journal kept the roll call. Nearly every member listed voted ay; Partridge voted no, and Ellery's no was recorded as "changed into ay at the request of the Member"; the journal does not say which member. On the 22nd the states present were Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia and North Carolina, with one member each from New Hampshire and South Carolina. And on the day of the audience itself, the 23rd, Congress resolved to write at once to the executives of New Hampshire, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, South Carolina and Georgia, demanding the immediate attendance of their delegates: during the sitting at this place there had never been more than seven states represented, most of them by only two delegates, and the ratification of the definitive treaty, among other matters, required the assent of at least nine states.
议定的接见次序共六条，前三条管入场与就座。第一条：议长与议员就座，并且戴着帽子，秘书立于议长身旁。第二条：将军到达时，由传信人通报秘书，秘书随即引入将军及其随行副官进入会议厅。第三条：将军由秘书引导至座位，落座，两侧各立一名副官，秘书回到自己的位置。坐着的、戴帽的、站着的、入场的，各有各的位置。

The agreed order ran to six clauses; the first three covered entry and seating. First, the President and the members were to sit, covered — that is, wearing their hats — with the secretary standing at the President's side. Second, the General's arrival was to be announced by a messenger to the secretary, and the secretary would then introduce the General, attended by his aides, into the Hall of Congress. Third, the secretary would conduct the General to a chair and he would be seated, an aide standing on either side of him, while the secretary resumed his own place. Sitters, hat-wearers, standers, entrants: everyone had an assigned position.

后三条写讲话与交接。待旁听者安顿好，必要时由秘书宣布肃静，议长对将军说：“阁下，合众国国会已准备好听取您的陈述。”将军起身讲话，然后坐下；议长宣读国会的答词，将军站着听；最后秘书把答词副本交给将军，收下委任状，将军告辞。日志所印的这份议定稿留着改动的痕迹：在讲委任状和讲稿副本交给谁的那一句，正文写的是把讲稿副本交给他的副官，再呈给秘书；“委任状”与“交给议长”都在方括号里，是后加的增字。编者注说，这份报告是埃尔布里奇·格里的笔迹，方括号里的字出自埃利亚斯·博迪诺之手。

The last three clauses dealt with the speech and the handover. After a proper time for the spectators to settle, silence was to be ordered by the secretary if necessary, and the President was to address the General in set words: "Sir, The United States in Congress assembled are prepared to receive your communications." The General would rise, speak and sit again; the President would deliver the answer of Congress, which the General was to receive standing; and the secretary would hand him a copy of the answer and receive the commission, after which the General would take his leave. The draft as printed carries changes. In the sentence about the commission and the copy of the address, the text has the copy of the address going to his aide to be presented to the secretary; both "[his Commission and a]" and "[to the President]" are bracketed insertions. The editors note that the report is in the writing of Elbridge Gerry, "the words in brackets being in the writing of Elias Boudinot".
他落座之后，会场宣布肃静。议长停顿了片刻，才告诉他：合众国国会已准备好听取他的陈述。他随即起身发言。那片刻停顿被写进了官方记录。

Once he was seated, silence was ordered, and the President paused before telling him that the United States in Congress assembled were prepared to receive his communications. The journal puts it this way: "the President, after a pause, informed him, that the United States in Congress assembled, were prepared to receive his communications". The pause made it into the record. Then the General rose and spoke.
说完，他走上前，把委任状和讲稿副本一并交给议长。委任状是权力的凭证，副本是这番说法的书面文本，两件东西一次交清。议定稿这一步留有方括号改动的痕迹，日志记下的结果是：由他本人走上前，交到议长手里。

With that, he stepped forward and placed his commission, together with a copy of his address, in the President's hands. The journal closes the entry in one line: "He then advanced and delivered to the President his commission, with a copy of his address". The commission was the token of authority; the copy was the written text of what he had said. Two objects, delivered at once. The draft at this step carries bracketed changes; what the journal records is that he himself stepped forward and put the commission into the President's hands.
作者推断，这套流程的要害在于它不依赖任何人相信谁的品格：仪式前一日成文，次日按议定次序进行，凭证当场易手，讲稿副本随凭证一并交出。（据日志，委任状是交给议长的，而议定稿第6条写的是由秘书接收，两者并不完全一致。）一个人是否忠诚，一场仪式无法证明；但权力是否已归位，可以在这一天被记成白纸黑字。这是作者对记录方式的解释，日志本身并未陈述其用意。

The author's inference is that the point of the procedure was that it depended on nobody's character. The order was written the day before and followed the next day, the token changed hands on the spot, and a copy of the address was handed over along with it. (The journal has the commission delivered to the President, whereas clause 6 of the draft has the secretary receiving it, so the two do not match exactly.) A man's loyalty cannot be proven by a ceremony. Whether power has been put back where it belongs, however, can be entered in black and white on a particular day. That is an interpretation of how the record was made; the journal itself states no such intention.
作者认为，把这次交还和一般的口头表态分开看，可以看出三件事同时在进行。其一，次序是事先写定的：22日议定，23日执行。其二，礼节是不对称的：将军起身致辞和退场时鞠躬，国会以脱帽回礼，站着的鞠躬、坐着的回礼，高低位差被保留了下来。其三，交出的是实物——委任状，外加讲稿副本。仪式、姿态、凭证三者叠加，才构成这一次有记录的权力交还。

As the author reads it, setting this handover beside an ordinary spoken one shows three things happening at once. First, the sequence was fixed in advance: agreed on the twenty-second, carried out on the twenty-third. Second, the etiquette was asymmetric: the General was to bow when he rose to speak and when he withdrew, and Congress to answer by uncovering: the standing man bowed, the seated body answered. The vertical distance between them was kept visible. Third, what changed hands was physical: the commission, plus a copy of the address. Ceremony, posture, and token together make up this documented transfer of power.
还有一层（作者的解读）：接受这份辞呈的国会，就“七个州是否有权接受”专门表决过一次——出席的只有七个州；接见当天，它还在写信催缺席的州派人来。在这样的时候，一套事先写定、公开执行、当场留档的程序，也许正替一个人手不齐的机构撑住了分量。日志没有把这几件事联系起来，这是作者的连接。

There is another layer, and it is the author's reading. The Congress receiving this resignation took a formal vote on whether seven states were competent to receive it: only seven states were present; on the very day of the audience it was still writing to absent states to send their delegates. At such a moment a procedure written in advance, carried out in public and recorded on the spot may have lent weight to a body short of hands. The journal does not connect these things; the connection is the author's.
全部事实来自《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录（1783年12月20日的来信、议决与关于七州权限的表决，12月22日议定的接见次序，12月23日的接见与华盛顿讲话文本）。没有在场者私人记述可对照，人物心情与现场反应不可知；议长答词未收入本篇证据包，本篇不引用；带括号改动的是接见次序的议定稿；材料经OCR识别，存在讹字，引文只取清晰片段；议定稿的删改在OCR文本中只能看到方括号内的字样。

All facts come from the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 (the letter, resolution and vote on whether seven states were competent, of December 20, 1783; the order of audience agreed on December 22; the audience and Washington's address of December 23). No private account by anyone present was available for comparison, so mood and reaction in the room are unknowable; the President's reply is not in this article's evidence pack and is not quoted here; the draft bearing bracketed changes is the protocol of the order of audience; the material was captured by OCR from a facsimile and contains misreadings, so quotations take only clean stretches; in the draft protocol the OCR shows only the bracketed insertions, not what was struck out.

dispositions.rationale: 中英文都不再说是埃勒里本人提出改票请求。现在只照录日志的写法，并注明日志没有写明是哪位议员。

dispositions.rationale: 删去“上午”和“on the morning of”，改为“23日接见当天”和“on the day of the audience itself”。证据只有日期，没有时段。
删去“有议员动议”和“a motion”，改为日志记下一个付诸表决的问题。证据没有记载动议或提出者。
